_purpose: Phase 8B. Frozen protocol: does any volatility forecast predict realised-minus-implied variance (the payoff of a 30-day S&P 500 variance swap, approximated with the VIX) out of sample? Public FRED data only. Frictionless and not directly tradable: an upper bound on what option strategies built on these forecasts could achieve. Committed before any forecast is scored.
data: FRED SP500 (daily close, 16:00 ET) and VIXCLS (VIX close, 16:15 ET), downloaded by the script to data/fred/ (not committed); SHA-256 recorded

window.definition: for origin day t (a trading day): returns r_{t+1}..r_{t+n_t}, where t+n_t is the last trading day with date <= date_t + 30 calendar days (the VIX's 30-calendar-day horizon)
window.realised_total_variance: RV_t = sum of r_s^2 over the window (close-to-close log returns)
window.implied_total_variance: IV_t = (VIX_t / 100)^2 * 30 / 365 (VIX is annualised on a 365-day calendar basis and refers to 30 calendar days)
window.payoff: P_t = RV_t - IV_t (total variance units; a long variance swap with unit variance notional, before costs). Reported annualised by x 365/30 where noted
window.n_t_note: n_t (19-22) is fixed by the exchange calendar, so it is known at t

forecasts_of_RV_t.hist: average r^2 over the last 21 days x n_t
forecasts_of_RV_t.garch: GARCH(1,1) on up to the last 1000 returns, refitted every 21 origins; sum of the n_t one-to-n_t-step variance forecasts
forecasts_of_RV_t.har: OLS of log(RV_s / n_s) on [1, log of average r^2 over the last 1, 5, 22 days at s], using only origins s whose window ended by t (expanding; refitted every 21 origins); forecast exp(mu + s_e^2/2) x n_t
forecasts_of_RV_t.chronos: amazon/chronos-2 zero-shot on the trailing 21-day realised-volatility series (annualised, last 512 values), prediction length 21, step-21 quantiles at the 21 native levels; E[Y^2] from the quantile function (Phase 7D) / 252 x n_t
forecasts_of_RV_t.chronos-vix: as chronos with VIX as a past-only covariate
forecasts_of_RV_t.comb: equal-weight mean of garch, har and chronos-vix (fixed in advance)

signal: s_t = F_t - IV_t for each forecaster
payoff_forecast: P_hat_t = a_t + b_t s_t with (a_t, b_t) from OLS on all past origins whose window ended by t (at least 250); no-signal benchmark P_bar_t = mean of the same past payoffs

development: first origin with 512 + 22 prior returns and 250 calibration origins
holdout: last origin with a complete window
periods.purge: development origins whose window extends into the holdout are dropped from development statistics
periods.use: development is descriptive; every pass/fail criterion is evaluated on the holdout only

inference.overlap: daily origins with ~21-trading-day windows overlap; all tests use Newey-West HAC variances with 21 lags or a moving-block bootstrap with block length 21 and 2000 resamples
inference.multiple_testing: Holm correction across the 7 forecasters (hist, ewma, garch, har, chronos, chronos-vix, comb) for V1 and V2

regimes: ex-ante VIX terciles with cut-offs from the development period's VIX distribution

hypotheses.V1: Predictability: the out-of-sample R^2 of P_hat over the no-signal benchmark is positive on the holdout, by a one-sided Clark-West test (HAC, 21 lags) at Holm-adjusted 5% across the 7 forecasters. The study 'passes' if at least one forecaster does.
hypotheses.V2: Direction: the hit rate of sign(P_hat) exceeds the no-signal benchmark's hit rate on the holdout (block-bootstrap one-sided p-value, Holm-adjusted 5%).
hypotheses.V3: Chronos-2 adds information beyond GARCH: adding s_chronos-vix to a payoff regression on s_garch improves out-of-sample MSPE on the holdout (one-sided Clark-West, 5%).
hypotheses.V4: Descriptive: out-of-sample R^2 by VIX tercile, holdout and development.
hypotheses.V5: Sanity: the mean payoff is negative (a variance risk premium) in development and holdout (HAC t-test, one-sided 5%).

also_reported: QLIKE of each F_t against RV_t (development, holdout, post-release)
calibration: coverage of 80% intervals for RV_t (Chronos-2: its own quantiles; others: forecast x exp(empirical quantiles of log(RV/F)) over the previous 500 completed origins)
robustness: every V1 statistic with all information lagged one trading day (removes the 15-minute VIX timing advantage)

frictionless illustration only (no hypothesis): first origin of each month, long one variance-swap unit if P_hat > 0 else short, against always-short; mean, sd, Sharpe and worst month. Not tradable: the VIX is not a traded variance-swap strike, and there are no costs.
kill_criterion: If V1 fails (no forecaster predicts the payoff out of sample on the holdout), the public data give no support to strategies that trade forecast-minus-implied variance; Part E strategies would need an independent rationale.
